reference.source: Long Cases in Clinical Medicine (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
reference.pathophysiology: Chemo-nadir fevers with no neutrophils demand door-hour antipseudomonals while bulky tumours lyse into potassium phosphate uric storms for rasburicase fluids; band-like back pain with retention means steroid-loaded MRI and decompression, and SVC, tamponade and hypercalcaemia each carry their own rescue.
additionalDifferentials: Non-neutropenic sepsis versus disc versus PE versus dehydration by counts MRI echo and fluids
TLS versus renal failure versus rhabdomyolysis by uric phosphate and CK
Cord compression versus transverse myelitis versus Guillain-Barre by level MRI and CSF
additionalInvestigations: Whole-spine MRI with calcium echo screens
